Vampire Count — ageless sovereign of midnight estates, his cold beauty a weapon, his hunger older than the kingdoms he has outlasted.
Blood-King — crowned in crimson, ruling plague-touched dominions with aristocratic precision, his mercy extinct, his elegance immaculate and terrifying.
Cursed Crown-Prince — heir to a throne built on damnation, exquisitely mannered, carrying inherited darkness like a second coronation no ceremony could undo.
Dark Sorcerer-Lord — silk-robed master of forbidden architectures, his library holding spells that unmade lesser men, his smile promising beautiful catastrophe.
Byronic Revenant — returned from death still wearing his finery, contemptuous of mortality, devastatingly handsome, trailing grief and ruin through lamplit drawing rooms.
Vampire Progenitor-Elder — the first, the source, older than language, dressed in centuries-old velvet, his authority absolute and his patience geological in its depth.
Demon Prince — aristocracy of Hell wearing a nobleman's face, his courtly manners flawless, his nature utterly corrosive beneath the gorgeous surface.
Undying Emperor — he has buried dynasties and remembers the names of every fallen civilization, ruling still, his imperial bearing unmarked by passing millennia.
Gothic Archduke — lord of crumbling mountain territories, his manners impeccable, his estate a labyrinth of beautiful horrors, his guests rarely departing intact.
Warlock-Duke — sworn to powers that razed his soul and refined his intellect to lethal sharpness, conducting dark rites with the composure of a dinner host.
Fallen-Angel Prince — heaven's most luminous exile, his beauty now weaponized by corruption, moving through mortal courts like a catastrophe dressed in white.
Lich-Lord — his immortality purchased at the cost of warmth, yet his bearing remains regal, his bespoke darkness worn with the elegance of old money.
Shadow-Bishop — consecrated to inverted sacraments, his cathedral a monument to exquisite blasphemy, his vestments immaculate, his theology quietly destroying everything around him.
Opera-Phantom-Lord — sovereign of hidden depths, composing ruin with architectural genius, his obsession refined to an art form, his menace exquisitely scored.
Nosferatu-Aristocrat — ancient hunger sculpted into noble features, his court immaculate, his reputation pristine, his true nature a beautiful secret the invited never survive.
Damned Cardinal — robed in corrupted ecclesiastical splendor, his faith inverted and weaponized, blessing congregations with catastrophe, serene behind his cardinal-red authority.
Blood-Sorcerer Count — combining lineage and forbidden art into singular lethality, his estate a theatre of controlled horror, his experiments conducted with surgical refinement.
Midnight Palatine — ruler of territories where daylight is policy, not physics, his judicial authority absolute, his sentences creative and irrevocably final.
Cursed Philosopher-King — sought forbidden truth and received damnation as answer, now ruling with cold brilliance, his court a monument to magnificent catastrophe.
Undead Marquis — ancien-régime elegance preserved beyond guillotine and revolution, his manners pre-dating nations, his grievances aging alongside him, perfectly maintained.
Hellsing-Shadow — no hunter but hunted, ancient predator wearing aristocratic restraint like a leash he chose, power barely contained within flawless presentation.

Dark Alchemist-Prince — transformed his noble blood into something beyond mortality through elegant, terrible science, his laboratories indistinguishable from cathedral interiors of controlled damnation.
Vampire Archlord — presiding over entire bloodline dynasties, his authority generational, his presence the gravity around which lesser dark nobles orbit in reverent terror.
Gothic Warlock-Baron — his barony sustained by pacts older than its foundations, his hospitality legendary and lethal, his company the most dangerous luxury available.
Infernal Duke-Regent — governing in absence of a throne his master abandoned, his regency immaculate, his corruption institutional, his elegance the face of inherited catastrophe.
Vampire Count: ancient blood-lord who rules midnight castles with cold grace, his gaze older than empires and twice as lethal.
Vampire Progenitor-Elder: the first-made, whose very name erases lesser bloodlines, draped in centuries of silk and massacre.
Cursed Crown-Prince: a kingdom's heir bound by a throne-curse, magnificent and ruinous, bleeding darkness from every regal gesture.
Dark Sorcerer-Lord: a nobleman who traded his soul for dominion over storm and shadow, conducting ruin with aristocratic precision.
Byronic Revenant: returned from death's country unchanged in beauty, devastating in contempt, his romantic grandeur hiding something hollow and hungry.
Blood-King: sovereign of a realm where tributaries mean something literal, crimson-robed, serene-faced, absolute and merciless in his red governance.
Demon-Prince: half-infernal nobility who inherited both hellfire and manor-house, elegant at court, catastrophic when his mask finally slips.
Undying Emperor: ten-thousand-year ruler whose empire collapsed but whose iron will persists, cold and magnificent as a beautiful ruin.
Gothic Archduke: a titled lord of crumbling grandeur, whose duchy exists between the living world and somewhere considerably darker and colder.
Nosferatu-Elegant: ancient predatory hunger housed in flawless aristocratic form, the monstrousness entirely concealed beneath immaculate cravat and courtly manners.
Shadow-Bishop: a prince of the church who found older theology underground, performing rites that predate scripture with ceremonial exactitude and black authority.
Opera-Phantom-Lord: genius-cursed nobleman commanding his underground domain with absolute aesthetic tyranny, beautiful enough to worship, dangerous enough to genuinely fear.
Damned Cardinal: scarlet-robed ecclesiastical power made wholly corrupt, whose blessing poisons and whose excommunications carry genuine supernatural consequence.
Warlock-Duke: a landed lord who bent natural law through sheer aristocratic arrogance, his estate a monument to forbidden mastery.
Lich-Lord Elegant: death's sovereign in magnificent preservation, every gesture precise and measured, his intelligence undimmed, his mercy utterly extinct.
Fallen-Angel Prince: cast from celestial courts still wearing heaven's beauty like a blade, his pride intact, his grace now weaponized.
Crimson Scion: last heir of a vampiric dynasty, impeccably dressed amid ancestral carnage, carrying bloodline obligations that demand terrible satisfactions.
Infernal Marquis: his title granted by courts below rather than above, conducting hellish diplomacy with the exquisite manners of a born courtier.
Plague-Lord Aristocrat: ancient noble who survived the Black Death by becoming something the plague itself respects, refined and quietly annihilating.
Dark Philosopher-Prince: a nobleman whose intellectual pursuit of forbidden truth left him magnificent, isolated, and fundamentally altered beyond human moral reach.
Necromancer-Earl: commands ancestral dead with the casual authority of a man reviewing household accounts, elegant lord of his own private nation of corpses.
Obsidian Throne-Holder: ruler of a kingdom that exists in permanent supernatural winter, his authority absolute as cold and twice as permanent.
Velvet Tyrant: governs with impeccable taste and zero mercy, his cruelty delivered in polished sentences and unhurried gestures of devastating consequence.
Accursed Palatine: a count whose bloodline carries divine punishment as naturally as coat-of-arms, wearing damnation with aristocratic composure and magnificent fatalism.
Mirror-Lord Revenant: lord of reflected worlds and dark glass-kingdoms, his handsomeness perfectly preserved and utterly predatory, ruling geometries that swallow light.
Vampire Progenitor Elder — the first and darkest, his veins holding the original curse, every descendant merely an echo of his terrible magnificence.
Cursed Crown Prince — heir to a damned dynasty, his regal bearing unbroken even as the black inheritance slowly consumes what remains of his soul.
Blood King — sovereign of a crimson court, his throne lacquered with the covenant of sacrifice, his dominion absolute and breathtakingly, terrifyingly beautiful.
Nosferatu-but-Elegant — the plague made beautiful, his aristocratic refinement a deliberate inversion of horror, the monster choosing opera gloves over the rawness of teeth.
Shadow Bishop — corrupted shepherd of a black cathedral, his sermons gilded heresy, vestments immaculate, voice resonant with the authority of something far older than God.
Opera Phantom Lord — architectural obsession and musical genius twisted into dominion, his realm underground and absolute, his presence a masterwork of terror and longing.
Warlock Duke — his estate a nexus of forbidden geometry, every room a working, his title legitimate but his power drawn from pacts no living court would ratify.
Lich-Lord Elegant — undeath refined into philosophy, his skeletal truth concealed beneath flawless glamour, the decay inside only perceptible as a faint chill in magnificent rooms.
Fallen Angel Prince — grace inverted into sovereignty, his beauty the remnant of heaven worn as a crown of irony, command natural as breathing, mercy long discarded.
Vampiric Archmage — he conquered mortality through blood and scholarship both, his library a catacomb of stolen centuries, his intellect the sharpest blade in a dark collection.
Night-Court Sovereign — absolute ruler of a realm that exists between dusk and dawn, his edicts beautiful and binding, his judgment delivered without warmth or hesitation.
Cursed Alchemist-Prince — his experiments purchased immortality at the cost of his humanity, porcelain composure concealing the monstrous transaction he completed in a gilded laboratory.
Obsidian Warlord-Noble — conquest refined into ceremony, his campaigns conducted with the precision of a maestro, violence elevated to something cold, deliberate, and disturbingly aesthetic.
Revenant Duke — murdered and returned with interest, his revenge patient and architectural, every move a note in a composition the living will not understand until the finale.
Eldritch Patrician — his bloodline touched by something beyond demonic, his drawing room pleasantries impeccable, the wrongness only visible in how the shadows pool around his chair.
Plague-Lord Baron — he carries pestilence as other men carry titles, his devastating appearance the beautiful lie that brings the unwise close enough for ruin.

Infernal Count Palatine — administrator of a hellish jurisdiction with meticulous bureaucratic grace, his damnation organized, his evil exquisitely procedural, his authority immovably, magnificently total.
Crimson Heir Eternal — the last of a dynasty that should have ended, his inheritance a curse worn like couture, devastating in aspect, utterly beyond salvation or surrender.
Vampire Count: Ancient bloodlord of crumbling castles, porcelain-pale and imperious, whose crimson gaze strips centuries of pretense bare.
Vampire Progenitor-Elder: First of his cursed lineage, immaculate in black velvet, older than kingdoms, colder than the graves he fills.
Cursed Crown Prince: A doomed heir enthroned in shadow, his beauty carved from grief, his kingdom rotting beautifully beneath his iron glove.
Dark Sorcerer-Lord: Silk-robed architect of forbidden cosmologies, his long fingers tracing ruin into existence with exquisite, unhurried deliberation.
Byronic Revenant: Returned from damnation magnificent and unrepentant, his brooding magnificence a wound the living cannot stop pressing against.
Blood-King: He rules not by divine right but by the iron mathematics of bloodshed, magnificent on his red-stained obsidian throne.
Demon Prince: Hellborn nobility made flesh, impeccably tailored darkness wearing a man's beautiful face like the finest conceivable disguise.
Undying Emperor: Ten thousand years of absolute dominion have refined his cruelty to a razor's philosophical edge, exquisitely patient.
Gothic Archduke: Master of fog-choked provinces and baroque ancestral estates, his courtesy more dangerous than any drawn blade.
Nosferatu-Elegant: The ancient hunger wearing perfect aristocratic form, devastatingly composed, his handsome stillness the stillness of a predator coiled.
Shadow Bishop: Ordained in darkness, robed in ecclesiastical splendor gone black, dispensing damnation from a cathedral carved from living shadow.
Opera Phantom-Lord: He composed the requiem of your civilization and now conducts its performance from his velvet throne below the earth.
Damned Cardinal: His crimson vestments conceal older allegiances than Rome's, his blessing a beautiful curse delivered with devastating pastoral warmth.
Warlock Duke: Aristocratic sorcerer whose ancestral grimoire is bound in the skin of former rivals, consulted with immaculate silver fingertips.
Lich-Lord Elegant: Death's sovereign, still magnificent, his skeletal truth hidden beneath flawless glamour and the scent of preserved funeral roses.
Fallen Angel Prince: Expelled from heaven's hierarchy, he descended with his beauty intact and his contempt for mortality perfectly crystallized.
Eternal Vampire Count: Centuries have stripped away sentiment, leaving only the magnificent architecture of his appetite and devastating formal manners.
Cursed Philosopher-King: He sought immortality through forbidden intellect, and now rules an empire of corpses, brilliant and irreparably damned.
Black Prince Revenant: Slain in treachery and returned with interest, his aristocratic composure concealing a vengeance older than his own kingdom.
Sanguine Archprince: Born of the first vampire's blood, he moves through mortal courts like a beautiful catastrophe dressed in Venetian black.
Infernal Duke: His family signed the compact with Hell generations ago; he simply inherited the estate, the title, and the obligation.
Gothic Vampire Sovereign: He does not hunt; mortality comes to him, drawn irresistibly by the gravity of his terrible, gorgeous presence.
Obsidian Necromancer-Lord: His armies require no wages and no sleep, and he reviews them from horseback at midnight, immaculately gloved.
Byronic Dark Overlord: Intellectually magnificent, morally annihilated, he governs his conquered territories with the same cold precision he applies to poetry.
Crimson Warlock Patriarch: Patriarch of a dynasty built on blood compacts and broken angels, still handsome, still hungry, utterly without remorse.
